status_note: Drafted from the UP Startup Atlas policy research (raw/L5_policy/compliance_calendar.csv), which checked each rule on 1 October 2026 against the India Code text and the gazette notifications cited below. A review on 27-28 October 2026 re-checked the rules against the primary texts named in each rule's verified_against, corrected the rules that carry a changed_on date (the change_note says what changed and why), and added the overrides below. Design 7.4 requires a CA partner to confirm these rules before any of them is used in a message: until confirmed_by and confirmed_on are filled in, the engine computes the calendar for the Admin pages only and marks every lead's needs as unconfirmed. verified_on is the engine team's check of the source, not the CA's confirmation.

anchors.incorporation: The date of incorporation in the MCA record.
anchors.company_first_fy_end: Companies Act 2013 s.2(41): a company's first financial year ends on 31 March of the year after it is incorporated (for a company incorporated on or after 1 January, the period runs to 31 March of the following year).
anchors.llp_first_fy_end: LLP Act 2008 s.2(1)(l): the first financial year ends on the 31 March after registration; an LLP registered after 30 September may choose to end it a year later (rules carry a note for LLPs registered from October to March).
anchors.first_tax_year_end: The first tax year of a new business ends on the 31 March after it is set up (Income-tax Act 2025 s.3(2)). A first year that ends on or before 31 March 2026 is a 'previous year' of the Income-tax Act 1961, which still governs that year's return; rules with by_tax_year say so.

overrides.note: For tax year 2025-26 (assessment year 2026-27) the CBDT extended the due date for companies and other audit cases from 31 October to 21 November 2026 (announced 28 September 2026; the formal order was to follow, and its number should be added once the CA has it).
For tax year 2025-26 an LLP whose accounts must be audited had until 21 November 2026 (CBDT extension announced 28 September 2026); the date shown is the one for an LLP that needs no audit.

rules.title: Hold the first board meeting

notes_by_type.OPC: With only one director no meeting is held: the director's resolution, entered in the minute book within the 30 days, does the business of the first meeting (s.122(5)). The first auditor must still be appointed within 30 days (s.139(6)).

conditional_for.NPL: For a Section 8 company, G.S.R. 466(E) of 5 June 2015 (as amended by G.S.R. 584(E) of 13 June 2017) applies s.173(1) only to the extent of one board meeting in every six calendar months, if its financial statements and annual returns are not in default. Whether a first meeting within 30 days is still required needs a CA's view.

rules.why: The first meeting appoints the first auditor, approves share certificates and opens the bank account.
rules.penalty: No specific penalty for the meeting itself; the general penalty of s.450 applies (₹10,000 plus ₹1,000 a day, up to ₹2 lakh for the company). Start-ups, OPCs and small companies pay half (s.446B).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.173(1), s.173(5), s.122(5); the Section 8 exemption from a secondary compilation only
rules.change_note: The OPC note cited the s.173(5) proviso, which only disapplies s.173(5) and s.174; the relief is s.122(5). Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added; for Section 8 companies the rule is marked conditional because of G.S.R. 466(E).

rules.title: Appoint the first statutory auditor
rules.why: If the board misses it, the members must appoint one at an extraordinary general meeting within 90 days.
rules.penalty: Fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh for the company and ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh for each officer in default (s.147(1)).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.139(6) and s.147(1)
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added: s.139(6) applies to every company other than a Government company.

rules.title: Issue share certificates to the subscribers

form_by_type.PLC: Credit to the subscribers' demat accounts (no paper certificate)

notes_by_type.PLC: An unlisted public company issues its shares only in dematerialised form (Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules 2014 r.9A); the CA should confirm how the two-month period is met through the depository.

conditional_for.NPL: Only if the company has a share capital: a Section 8 company limited by guarantee has no shares to certify.

rules.why: Required within two months of incorporation for every subscriber to the memorandum.
rules.penalty: ₹50,000 for the company and for each officer in default (s.56(6)); start-ups, OPCs and small companies pay half (s.446B).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.56(4)(a); r.9A not re-read in this review
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added; Section 8 marked conditional on having a share capital; public companies noted as demat-only.

rules.title: File the declaration for commencement of business

conditional_for.NPL: Only if the company has a share capital (s.10A(1) applies to a company 'having a share capital').

rules.why: The company cannot start business or borrow until it is filed; the registrar can begin striking off a company that has not filed it.
rules.penalty: ₹50,000 for the company and ₹1,000 a day for each officer in default, up to ₹1 lakh (s.10A(2)).
rules.law: Companies Act 2013 s.10A; Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014 r.23A
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added; Section 8 marked conditional on having a share capital.

rules.title: Hold the first annual general meeting
rules.why: Within nine months of the end of the first financial year. The annual filings below run from this date.
rules.penalty: Fine up to ₹1 lakh for the company and every officer in default, plus up to ₹5,000 a day while it continues (s.99).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.96(1), s.99 and s.2(41)
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added: s.96(1) applies to every company other than an OPC.

rules.title: Appoint the auditor at the first AGM and inform the registrar
rules.why: The first auditor serves only until the first AGM, which appoints an auditor for five years.
rules.penalty: Fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh for the company and ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh for each officer in default (s.147(1)), plus the registrar's late fee.
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.147(1); the 15 days are in the Audit Rules r.4(2), not re-read in this review

rules.title: Appoint the auditor for five years and inform the registrar
rules.condition: An OPC holds no AGM, so its member appoints the auditor for five years by a resolution entered in the minute book (s.122(3)-(4)), normally when the first financial statements are adopted (they are due by 27 September after the first financial year). ADT-1 is filed within 15 days of that resolution.
rules.penalty: Fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh for the company and ₹10,000 to ₹1 lakh for each officer in default (s.147(1)), plus the registrar's late fee.
rules.law: Companies Act 2013 s.139(1), s.122(3)-(4), s.147(1); Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014 r.4(2)
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.122 and s.147(1)
rules.change_note: New rule: the calendar had no auditor appointment for OPCs after the first auditor.

rules.title: File the first financial statements
rules.why: Within 30 days of the AGM (or of the date it should have been held).
rules.penalty: ₹10,000 plus ₹100 a day, up to ₹2 lakh for the company (s.137(3)), plus the registrar's late fee; start-ups and small companies pay half (s.446B).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.137(1) and s.446B

rules.title: File the first financial statements
rules.why: An OPC holds no AGM; it files within 180 days of the end of the financial year.
rules.penalty: ₹10,000 plus ₹100 a day, up to ₹2 lakh for the company (s.137(3)); OPCs pay half (s.446B).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of the s.137(1) proviso for OPCs

rules.title: File the first annual return

notes_by_type.PLC: A public company is never a small company (s.2(85)), so it files MGT-7.
notes_by_type.NPL: A Section 8 company is never a small company (s.2(85) proviso), so it files MGT-7.

rules.penalty: ₹10,000 plus ₹100 a day, up to ₹2 lakh for the company and ₹50,000 for each officer (s.92(5)); start-ups and small companies pay half (s.446B).
rules.law: Companies Act 2013 s.92(4)-(5); Companies (Management and Administration) Rules 2014 r.11
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.92(4)-(5) and s.2(85)
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added, with MGT-7 as their form.

rules.title: File the first annual return
rules.why: An OPC holds no AGM; in practice it files within 60 days of 30 September.
rules.penalty: ₹10,000 plus ₹100 a day, up to ₹2 lakh for the company (s.92(5)); OPCs pay half (s.446B).
rules.verified_against: India Code text of s.92(4); the 30 September reference date is practice (the earlier of the readings), for the CA to confirm

rules.title: File the first income-tax return

form_by_type.NPL: ITR-6, or ITR-7 if the company is registered for the charitable exemption

rules.why: Every company files every year, profit or loss: by 31 October after the tax year (30 November if a transfer-pricing report is needed).
rules.penalty: Late fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh) under s.428, plus interest.

by_tax_year.law: Income-tax Act 1961 s.139(1), s.234F (the Income-tax Act 2025 applies from tax year 2026-27)
by_tax_year.penalty: Late fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh) under s.234F of the 1961 Act, plus interest.

rules.verified_against: Income-tax Bill 2025 as passed (s.3, s.263, s.428); Budget 2026 memorandum (which Act governs which year); CBDT extension of 28 September 2026 (see overrides)
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added. A first tax year ending on or before 31 March 2026 now cites the Income-tax Act 1961, and the CBDT extension to 21 November 2026 for that year is applied as an override.

rules.title: File the return of money received that is not a deposit
rules.condition: Only if the company has received money such as director loans, convertible notes or share application money outstanding on 31 March.
rules.penalty: Fine up to ₹5,000 plus up to ₹500 a day for the company and every officer in default (r.21), plus the registrar's late fee.
rules.law: Companies Act 2013 s.73-76; Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules 2014 r.16, r.16A, r.21
rules.verified_against: Not re-read against the Deposits Rules in the October review
rules.change_note: Public (PLC) and Section 8 (NPL) companies added. As a conditional rule it is now shown as 'if it applies' and never counted as a firm deadline.

rules.title: Register for GST once liable
rules.condition: Within 30 days of becoming liable: in Uttar Pradesh, aggregate turnover above ₹20 lakh, or above ₹40 lakh if the business supplies only goods (the ₹40 lakh limit does not cover ice cream, pan masala or tobacco). Inter-State supplies of goods and some other cases need registration at once, whatever the turnover (s.24). Sellers on e-commerce platforms often must register regardless of turnover, but some are exempt below the limit: a CA must confirm which applies, as this exemption was not checked against its notification in the October review.
rules.penalty: ₹10,000 or the tax evaded, whichever is higher (CGST Act s.122(1)(xi)).
rules.law: CGST Act 2017 s.22, s.24, s.25; Notification 10/2019-Central Tax
rules.verified_against: Notification 10/2019-Central Tax (the list of excluded States does not include Uttar Pradesh; goods excluded from the ₹40 lakh limit)
rules.change_note: Added the goods excluded from the ₹40 lakh limit, and flagged the e-commerce case for the CA instead of saying all e-commerce sellers must register at once.

rules.title: Directors' KYC
rules.advisory: Since 31 March 2026 every DIN holder files KYC once every three financial years, by 30 June; the year depends on each director's own cycle. A change of mobile number, email or address must be reported within 30 days.
rules.penalty: The DIN is deactivated until KYC is filed with a fee.
rules.law: Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 r.12A, as substituted by G.S.R. 943(E) dated 31 December 2025
rules.verified_against: Gazette text of G.S.R. 943(E): substituted r.12A(1)-(2), in force 31 March 2026

rules.title: File the LLP agreement
rules.why: Without a filed agreement, the default terms of the Act's First Schedule govern the partners.
rules.penalty: Registrar's additional fee of ₹100 a day of delay, with no cap.
rules.law: LLP Act 2008 s.23(2), s.23(4); LLP Rules 2009 r.21
rules.verified_against: Not re-read against the LLP Rules in the October review

rules.title: File the statement of account and solvency
rules.notes_if_late_registration: If the LLP chose a longer first year, this is a year later.
rules.notes_if_jan_mar_registration: Registered between January and March, the LLP's first financial year ends on this 31 March unless it could choose to end it a year later under the proviso to s.2(1)(l) (registration 'after the 30th day of September'), which is not settled for January to March: a CA should confirm before this date is relied on.
rules.penalty: ₹100 a day for the LLP and its designated partners, up to ₹1 lakh (LLP) and ₹50,000 (each partner) (s.34(5)); no penalty if the default is put right before, or within 30 days of, the adjudicating officer's notice (s.76A(1), first proviso); start-up and small LLPs pay half (s.76A(1), second proviso).
rules.verified_against: LLP (Amendment) Act 2021: substituted s.34(5) and inserted s.76A; the 30 October date is r.24, not re-read in this review
rules.change_note: The half-penalty cited s.76A(3); it is the second proviso to s.76A(1). Added the first proviso (no penalty if put right within 30 days of the notice) and a note for LLPs registered from January to March.

rules.title: File the annual return
rules.notes_if_late_registration: If the LLP chose a longer first year, this is a year later.
rules.notes_if_jan_mar_registration: Registered between January and March, the LLP's first financial year ends on this 31 March unless it could choose to end it a year later under the proviso to s.2(1)(l) (registration 'after the 30th day of September'), which is not settled for January to March: a CA should confirm before this date is relied on.
rules.penalty: ₹100 a day for the LLP and its designated partners, up to ₹1 lakh (LLP) and ₹50,000 (each partner) (s.35(2)); no penalty if the default is put right before, or within 30 days of, the adjudicating officer's notice (s.76A(1), first proviso); start-up and small LLPs pay half (s.76A(1), second proviso).
rules.law: LLP Act 2008 s.35, s.76A(1); LLP Rules 2009 r.25
rules.verified_against: LLP (Amendment) Act 2021: substituted s.35(2) and inserted s.76A; the 60 days are r.25, not re-read in this review
rules.change_note: The half-penalty cited s.76A(3); it is the second proviso to s.76A(1). Added the first proviso and a note for LLPs registered from January to March.

rules.title: File the first income-tax return
rules.note: The date shown is for an LLP whose accounts need no audit. If they must be audited (LLP Rules r.24(8): turnover above ₹40 lakh or contribution above ₹25 lakh, or a tax audit), the date is 31 October, and 30 November with a transfer-pricing report.
rules.why: Every LLP files every year, profit or loss: by 31 August after the tax year if its accounts need no audit (Finance Act 2026), otherwise by 31 October.
rules.penalty: Late fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh) under s.428, plus interest.
rules.law: Income-tax Act 2025 s.263(1)(a), s.263(1)(c) as amended by the Finance Act 2026, s.428

by_tax_year.law: Income-tax Act 1961 s.139(1) Explanation 2 as amended by the Finance Act 2026, s.234F (the Income-tax Act 2025 applies from tax year 2026-27)
by_tax_year.penalty: Late fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh) under s.234F of the 1961 Act, plus interest.

rules.verified_against: Budget 2026 memorandum ('Rationalising due dates for filing of return of Income': 31 August for non-audit business cases and partners of non-audit firms, from AY 2026-27 under the 1961 Act and tax year 2026-27 under the 2025 Act), and the Income Tax Department's reminder of the 31 August 2026 date; the enacted Finance Act text was not read, so the CA should confirm it
rules.change_note: Was 31 July. The Finance Act 2026 moved non-audit business returns (an LLP is a firm) to 31 August; audited LLPs stay at 31 October. A first tax year ending on or before 31 March 2026 now cites the Income-tax Act 1961.
